items.stem:
Plants → Deer → Lion
In the given food chain, what will be the impact of removing all the organisms of second trophic level on the first and third trophic level? Will the impact be the same for the organisms of the third trophic level in the above food chain if they were present in a food web? Justify.
items.answer: Plants → Deer → Lion. If we remove the deer from the second trophic level, the population of plants will drastically increase while the population of lions will decrease. No, the impact will not be the same in a food web, because a food web contains many other alternative food sources which increase the stability of the ecosystem, so it is easy to overcome a disturbance in it.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the food-chain arrows and printed them as '$$'; restored as → in both the stem and the answer.

items.stem: Write the percentage of (i) solar energy captured by the autotrophs and (ii) energy transferred from autotrophs to the next level in a food chain.
items.answer: (i) The autotrophs capture about 1% of the solar energy that falls on their leaves for the process of photosynthesis. (ii) According to 'The 10% Rule' there is only 10% flow of energy from one trophic level to the next higher level, so only 10% of the energy will get transferred from the autotrophs to the herbivores.

items.stem: If a grasshopper is eaten by a frog, then the energy transfer will be from
items.answer: (c) primary consumer to secondary consumer. The grasshopper feeds on plants and is therefore a herbivore (primary consumer); the frog that eats the grasshopper is a secondary consumer, so energy flows from the primary consumer to the secondary consumer.

items.stem: Aquarium need to be cleaned once in a while whereas ponds or lakes do not require any cleaning. Explain.
items.answer: An aquarium needs to be cleaned because it is not a self-sustained natural ecosystem; it is a man-made or artificial ecosystem. Ponds and lakes are self-sustained natural ecosystems in which the nutrient cycle and the energy flow occur naturally.
items.ocr: Missing full stops after 'cleaning' and 'Explain' supplied; 'naturals' read as 'natural'.

items.stem: If a lake is contaminated with pesticides, which one of the following organisms will contain in its body the maximum concentration of pesticides and why? Small fish, Pelicans, Zooplanktons, Phytoplanktons, Big fish.
items.answer: Pelican birds will contain the maximum concentration of pesticides in their body, as they are at the highest trophic level (top consumer) in the food chain of the given organisms. This happens due to biomagnification, i.e. the amount of harmful chemicals magnifies successively at the higher trophic levels.

items.stem: Consider the food chain: Grass → Deer → Lion. What will happen if lions are removed from the above food chain?
items.answer: Removal of the lion (carnivore) from the above food chain will cause a disturbance in the environmental balance and will increase the number of deer (herbivores) to such an extent that they will eat up the whole grass. The density of producers like grass will be very much reduced and this will turn the area into a desert, which eventually results in the death of all the deer due to lack of food.

items.stem: What are the heterotrophs?
items.answer: The organisms which cannot make their own food from raw materials such as CO₂, H₂O etc. using sunlight are called heterotrophs. Heterotrophs depend on other organisms for their food. All animals, including human beings, are heterotrophs. Heterotrophs are also termed as consumers.
items.ocr: 'CO $2$' and '$\mathrm{H_{2}O}$' rewritten as CO₂ and H₂O; the misprint 'hetetrotrophs' corrected to heterotrophs.

items.stem: What will happen to the garbage and dead animals and plants in absence of microorganisms?
items.answer: The garbage and the dead plants and animals will not decompose if there are no decomposers, i.e. saprophytic bacteria and fungi. The bodies cannot decay in the absence of bacteria or fungi and the nutrients will not get recycled.

items.stem: In a certain study conducted on occurrence of DDT along food chains in an ecosystem, the concentration of DDT in grass was found to be 0.5 ppm (parts per million), in sheep it was 2 ppm and in man it was 10 ppm. Why was the concentration of DDT maximum in case of man?
items.answer: DDT is a non-biodegradable chemical which gradually accumulates in the fatty tissue at each trophic level. Since man is at the highest trophic level, there is maximum accumulation of DDT in him. This happens due to biological magnification.

items.stem:
What are the producers? Give suitable examples.
Or
Define autotrophs.
items.answer: Producers or autotrophs are the organisms that can make their own food from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll. This process is called photosynthesis, in which producers convert sunlight into the form of food (chemical energy). Examples: green plants and algae are autotrophs or producers.

items.stem: What happens to the dead bodies?
items.answer: The microorganisms comprising bacteria and fungi break down the dead bodies into simpler forms and recycle the nutrients in the environment. These microorganisms are called decomposers.

items.stem: In a food chain comprising frogs, insects, birds and grass, which one of the organisms is likely to have maximum concentration of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals in its body?
items.answer: Birds would have the maximum concentration of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals in their body, as they occupy the topmost trophic level in the given food chain (grass → insects → frogs → birds). This happens due to biological magnification.

items.stem: Define food chain and write its two functions.
items.answer: The sequence of living organisms in which one organism consumes another to transfer food energy to the next trophic level is called a food chain. A food chain helps: (a) in maintaining energy flow and ecological balance, (b) in maintaining the interdependence of different organisms.

items.stem: What is biodiversity? What will happen if biodiversity of an area is not preserved? Mention one effect of it.
items.answer: Biodiversity is the existence of a wide variety of species of plants, animals and micro-organisms in a natural habitat within a particular environment, or the existence of genetic variation within a species. Biodiversity of an area is the number of species and the range of different life forms found there; forests are biodiversity hotspots. In an ecosystem every living being is dependent on another living being. If biodiversity is not maintained, the various links of the food chains go missing, and if one organism goes missing this will affect all the living beings that are dependent on it and the environmental balance will get disturbed.

items.stem: What will happen if all the carnivores are removed from the earth?
items.answer: If all the carnivores are removed from the earth, the population of herbivores will increase. The large population of herbivores will overgraze. As a result, all plants will disappear from the earth's surface and ultimately the earth may become a desert, and eventually all herbivores will die due to lack of food. The biosphere will get disturbed, which will lead to the end of life on earth.
items.ocr: 'if all the carnivore our are removed' read as 'if all the carnivores are removed'; 'die to lack of food' read as 'die due to lack of food'.

items.stem:
Which one of the following food habits is better and why?
(a) Plant → Man
(b) Plant → Goat → Man
items.answer: (a) Plant → Man is better. Reason: according to the ten percent law of nature, in a shorter food chain the maximum transfer of energy takes place, so more energy of the producer reaches man when he feeds directly on plants.

items.stem: Give some examples of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
items.answer: (a) Terrestrial ecosystem: a forest, a crop field, etc. (b) Aquatic ecosystem: a pond, a lake and an aquarium.

items.stem: What will happen to grasslands if all the grazers/herbivores are removed from there?
items.answer: If all the grazers/herbivores are removed from grasslands, grass will grow unchecked. It may help the growth of some organisms harmful to the animals and plants. Further, the animals which feed on the grazers will die of starvation. The biogeochemical cycle will stop and ultimately the whole biosphere will get disturbed.

items.stem: Name the sources from where the green plants obtain C, H and O.
items.answer: (a) Green plants get C, i.e. carbon, from the CO₂ present in the atmosphere. (b) H (hydrogen) and O (oxygen) are obtained from the water absorbed from the soil. (c) Oxygen is also obtained from the air.

items.stem: What would happen if all the decomposers were eliminated from the earth? Explain.
items.answer: Decomposers decompose the complex organic molecules present in dead plants and animals to the simple molecular level. Thus, decomposers help the return of various nutrients to the soil/water so that these are available to the producers once again. So, if decomposers are removed from the earth, the soil/water will become deficient in nutrients and the operation of the various mineral cycles will get affected.

items.stem:
Describe the structure of an ecosystem.
Or
What are the structural components of an ecosystem?
items.answer: An ecosystem consists of a non-living (abiotic) environment and a living (biotic) biological community. The non-living environment of an ecosystem consists of components like water, soil, light, carbon dioxide, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and other elements. The living community is made up of plants, animals and micro-organisms.

items.stem: Give two examples each of producers, consumers and decomposers.
items.answer: Producers: green plants such as the sugarcane plant, the wheat plant, etc. Consumers: animals such as cow, goat, etc. Decomposers: certain saprophytic bacteria and fungi. The microorganisms comprising bacteria and fungi break down the dead bodies into simpler forms and recycle nutrients in the environment; these microorganisms are called decomposers.

items.stem: What are the first order consumers?
items.answer: The animals which eat plants directly as their food are termed as primary or first order consumers. Therefore, herbivores are first order consumers.

items.stem: What are carnivores? Name a few of them.
items.answer: The organisms which feed only on animals are called carnivores or carnivorous animals. Lion, jackal, hawk, etc. are carnivorous animals.

items.stem: Draw a schematic diagram to show the food chains.
items.answer: A food chain is drawn as a straight-line sequence of trophic levels, with each arrow pointing from the organism that is eaten towards the organism that eats it. The printed diagram shows three such food chains: (a) Tree (plant) → Deer → Lion, (b) Plant → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle, and (c) Aquatic plants → Zooplankton (shrimp) → Fish → Crane. The producers occupy the first trophic level, the herbivores the second, and the carnivores the successive levels.

items.stem: Name different types of heterotrophs.
items.answer: There are four types of heterotrophs. These are: (a) Herbivores — these are also called primary or first order consumers. (b) Carnivores — these are also called secondary or second order consumers. (c) Omnivores. (d) Parasites.

items.stem: Write harmful effects of ultraviolet radiations.
items.answer: Harmful effects of ultraviolet radiations are as follows: (a) It causes skin cancer. (b) It causes sun burn. (c) It causes eye diseases like cataract.

items.answer: (i) 10 to 16 km. (ii) UV (ultraviolet) rays of the sun. (iii) Skin cancer.

items.stem: Larger animals kill the smaller animals in the forest, eat whatever they can, leave the rest in the forest but the forest is never found full of dead animals. What happens to the bodies of these dead animals?
items.answer: The bodies of the dead animals are acted upon by saprophytic bacteria and fungi, which break them down into simple nutrients. These nutrients are later released into the soil, which serves as a nutrient pool. From this pool, plants again use these nutrients for their growth and thus the nutrients get recycled.

items.stem: (a) What is the full form of (i) UNEP (ii) CFCs? (b) On what basis are organisms grouped as producers, consumers and decomposers? (c) Write two problems that would arise if there were no decomposers in an ecosystem.
items.answer: (a) (i) UNEP: United Nations Environment Programme. (ii) CFCs: Chlorofluorocarbons. (b) Organisms can be grouped as producers, consumers and decomposers according to the manner in which they obtain their nutrition from the environment. (c) Two problems that would arise in the absence of decomposers in an ecosystem are: (i) decomposition of garbage as well as of dead plants and animals will not take place; (ii) recycling of nutrients and natural replenishment of the soil will not take place.

items.stem: Give the characteristics of food chain.
items.answer: The characteristics of a food chain are the following: (i) A food chain always proceeds in a progressive straight line. (ii) A food chain helps in understanding the food relationship and the energy interactions among various organisms in an ecosystem. (iii) It helps to understand the movement of toxic substances in an ecosystem and the problem of their biological magnification.
